MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Better & Fairer Care. Always.

Become the UKG Capability Expert

Drive Workforce Excellence

Influence Continuous Improvement 

At St Vincent's, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As Australia's largest not-for-profit health and aged care provider, we are committed to delivering exceptional, compassionate care and improving health outcomes for communities across New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria.
 

Guided by our values of Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence, more than 30,000 employees come together each day to make a genuine difference. When you join St Vincent's, you'll become part of a purpose-driven organisation dedicated to shaping a better and fairer health and aged care system for all.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an experienced UKG Support Specialist - Training to play a pivotal role in building workforce capability and supporting one of Australia's largest healthcare organisations.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about workforce technology, user education and continuous improvement. You'll become the go-to expert for UKG system training, empowering managers and employees to confidently navigate workforce management processes while ensuring payroll accuracy, compliance and operational excellence.

Working closely with Payroll, HR and operational leaders, you'll deliver engaging training programs, develop practical learning resources and provide advanced system support that enhances the employee experience across St Vincent's.

What You'll Do

Deliver engaging UKG training sessions for managers, employees and new starters

Develop and maintain user guides, quick reference materials, FAQs and training documentation

Provide advanced support and guidance on UKG, including timecards, rosters, leave, approvals and payroll-related processes

Act as an escalation point for complex UKG enquiries and coach users to build confidence and self-sufficiency

Identify recurring issues and knowledge gaps, delivering targeted education to improve system capability

Promote consistent, compliant and best-practice use of UKG across the organisation

Support payroll accuracy by monitoring schedules, timecards and workforce management data

Contribute to system testing, process improvements and enhancements to training resources

Work collaboratively with Payroll, HR and key stakeholders to improve the user experience and system adoption

About You

You're an experienced workforce systems, payroll or systems support professional who enjoys helping others learn, solve problems and succeed.

Passionate about customer service, training and continuous improvement, you have the ability to translate complex system functionality into practical, easy-to-understand guidance that empowers users and builds confidence. You thrive on building strong stakeholder relationships, delivering engaging learning experiences and helping people get the very best from technology. With a proactive, solutions-focused mindset, you're motivated by improving processes, enhancing user capability and driving operational excellence.

Key Experience & Capability

Demonstrated experience supporting workforce management or payroll systems, ideally UKG-Kronos.

Experience designing and delivering system training, workshops or user education programs.

Strong understanding of rostering, time and attendance, payroll processes and workforce compliance.

Proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve complex system issues while coaching and empowering end users.

Excellent written communication skills with experience developing learning resources, user guides and process documentation.

Strong stakeholder engagement and customer service skills, with the ability to communicate confidently across all levels of the organisation.

Highly organised with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Experience supporting system testing, process improvement, change initiatives or workforce systems optimisation will be highly regarded.
 

Why St Vincent's?

Make a meaningful impact - Help empower thousands of employees and managers to confidently use one of our most critical workforce systems.

Work with purpose - Join a values-driven organisation guided by Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence.

Share your expertise - Lead training initiatives that improve system capability, payroll accuracy and workforce outcomes across a national organisation.

Enjoy great benefits - Access salary packaging, wellbeing initiatives, employee discounts and a range of additional benefits.

Be part of something bigger - Join a collaborative team committed to service excellence, innovation and continuous improvement.

Ready to Make an Impact? Apply now and help shape the future of workforce capability at St Vincent's Health Australia.
 

If you're passionate about workforce technology, user enablement and delivering exceptional customer experiences, we'd love to hear from you.

Please note applications will be reviewed as they are received, and the role may close early if a suitable candidate is identified.
 

For more information, contact TalentHealthVIC@svha.org.au.

Equal Opportunity

At St Vincent's we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued and empowered to thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, abilities, gender identities and life experiences.

Our workforce reflects the communities we serve, and we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger.

Location: Palmerston, Northern Territory
Employment type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: $67,510 to $72,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 91 213 951 452) is a takeaway food outlet located in a busy shopping centre food court in Palmerston, serving a range of freshly prepared takeaway meals, including loaded chips, fish and chips, fried chicken, seafood baskets, hotdogs, ice cream and milkshakes.

The successful applicant will oversee the outlet's front-of-house retail operations and support its smooth daily operation. 

About the Role
The Retail Supervisor will supervise and coordinate the activities of staff, maintain high customer service standards and assist management with staff supervision, stock control, cash handling and the day-to-day operation of the outlet. 

The position requires availability across a rotating roster, including weekends, public holidays and evening shifts where required.

Key Responsibilities
- Supervise and coordinate the daily activities of counter and staff.
- Allocate duties and prepare or assist with staff rosters.
- Ensure customers receive prompt, friendly and accurate service.
- Train staff in customer service, point-of-sale procedures, food handling and workplace requirements.
- Monitor staff performance and provide day-to-day guidance and support.
- Respond to customer enquiries, concerns and complaints.
- Operate and supervise point-of-sale and cash-handling procedures.
- Complete opening and closing procedures, including cash reconciliation.
- Monitor stock levels and assist with stocktaking and ordering.
- Receive and check deliveries against orders.
- Ensure menu items, promotional materials and prices are correctly displayed.
- Maintain the cleanliness and presentation of the service counter, customer areas and retail displays.
- Ensure food safety, workplace health and safety, security and hygiene procedures are followed.
- Report staffing, stock, equipment and operational issues to management.
- Assist with counter service and other operational duties during busy periods.

Skills and Experience
The successful applicant must have:
- At least one year of relevant experience in retail, takeaway food, fast food or a similar customer-service environment;
- Previous experience supervising or coordinating staff;
- Experience with point-of-sale systems, cash handling and daily reconciliations;
- Good customer service and complaint-handling skills;
- The ability to organise staff and prioritise duties during busy service periods;
- Knowledge of stock control and basic inventory procedures;
- Good communication and interpersonal skills;
- A reliable, organised and hands-on approach to work; and
- The ability to work weekends, public holidays and shifts according to the business roster.
- A current food-safety or food-handling certificate is desirable.

How to Apply
To apply, submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a busy and growing takeaway food business serving the Palmerston community, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Casual Community Support Worker WHD4-WHD3 - Elliston



 Apply now
 Job no: 944263

 Work type: Casual

 Location: Eyre and Western

 Categories: Catering and Hospitality, Community and Social Services, Child, Aged and Disability Care, Support Services





 

Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, Country Health Connect - Home Support 

Position based in Elliston

Salary:

WHD3: $32.90 - $33.72 per hour + 25% casual loading

WHD4: $34.58 - $35.27 per hour + 25% casual loading

Casual positions available until 30 June 2027, working over a 7 day roster

Please note that this position is multi-classified as either a WHD-3 or WHD-4.

Exciting Casual Opportunity: Community Support Worker 

On the remote Eyre Peninsula, in the coastal community of Elliston, the work of a Community Support Worker carries real weight. At Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN), you'll be the person who helps someone stay in the home they love - offering practical support, genuine connection, and the kind of care that makes independence possible.

What You'll Be Doing

Working within EFNLHN's Consumer Directed Care model, you'll deliver support shaped by each client's own goals and preferences - because here, the person receiving care guides the plan. Shifts, duties, and frequency reflect the needs of the people you support, giving your work real purpose and variety.

Assist clients with personal hygiene, grooming, and mobility in a respectful and dignified manner

Perform household tasks including cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and minor gardening

Provide reliable transport to appointments and community outings

Support social engagement and activities that contribute to client wellbeing

At the WHD4 level, deliver personal care to clients with more complex support needs

What You'll Bring

A warm, empathetic approach and the confidence to work independently in the community

Sound communication skills and genuine respect for people from diverse cultures and backgrounds

Experience supporting aged, frail, or disabled individuals

Ability to work collaboratively as part of a small, community-based team

Familiarity with SA Health's approach to community care, or willingness to learn EFNLHN's Consumer Directed Care model

For appointment at WHD4 level: Certificate III or higher in Individual Support (Aged Care, Disability, or Home and Community)

Life and Work in Elliston with EFNLHN

EFNLHN serves one of Australia's most geographically vast and distinctive regions, and Elliston sits at the edge of it - a tight-knit coastal community where your contribution is visible every single day. As a SA Health employee, you'll access salary packaging benefits that meaningfully increase your take-home pay, alongside the professional support of a broader health network that genuinely invests in its people. This is a casual role offering real flexibility, and the Consumer Directed Care model means your day-to-day work reflects the actual preferences of the people you serve - not a fixed, one-size-fits-all schedule. This position is available through to 30 June 2027.

Ready to Apply

The business is known for it's commitment to handcrafted meals, warm service, and consistent customer satisfaction. They are currently hiring for the following role: Barista. These roles offer a great opportunity to join a dynamic team and grow within a stable, fast-paced hospitality environment.

BARISTA
Job Overview:
As a Barista, you will be responsible for crafting high-quality coffee beverages while maintaining excellent service and station cleanliness in a fast-paced café setting.

Key Responsibilities:
Operate espresso machines and prepare coffee drinks to standard.
Provide prompt and friendly service to customers.
Maintain barista station cleanliness and stock levels.
Assist with light food handling as needed.

Requirements:
Prior experience as a Barista in a busy café environment.
Good knowledge of espresso equipment and coffee preparation.
Excellent customer service and multitasking ability.

Position: Office Manager 
Office Location: 60 South Street, Ipswich QLD 4305 
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent, Minimum 38 hours a week  
Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum (plus superannuation)

Our client PRITHVEER PTY LTD is an established Australian transport and logistics provider based out of Ipswich, Queensland, operating since 2014. They specialise in delivering goods across hospitality and healthcare sector, supported by a dedicated vehicle fleet delivering general freight, palletised freight, same-day/next-day services. They require dedicated experienced Office Manager to oversee the office and administrative backbone of the business.

Responsibilities
The Office Manager is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the daily administrative operations of the business, ensuring effective communication and workflow between office, warehouse, and fleet functions. The role involves developing and improving office systems, managing administrative staff, preparing rosters and schedules, recruitment and training, and maintaining efficient office resources. Manages budgets, financial records, and compliance requirements to support smooth freight operations, fleet administration, and the overall performance of the business.

Key Duties 
•	Plan, organise, direct and coordinate the day-to-day administrative operations of the business office, managing office procedures, correspondence, office records, and information flow between administration, dispatch, and fleet teams.
•	Develop, implement and review office systems, policies and administrative procedures to improve operational efficiency, document control, customer service processes, and internal communication across the business.
•	Liaise and coordinate with administrative staff and director, prepare workflow, and coordinate workload requirements to support freight, delivery, and business operations.
•	Oversee recruitment, onboarding, induction, and training coordination for office staffs, ensuring staff are appropriately supported and aligned with company procedures and operational requirements.
•	Maintain supplier records, and other administrative information systems to ensure accuracy, accessibility, and compliance with company requirements.
•	Manage office budgets, process financial administration activities, monitor expenditure, coordinate invoicing and accounts administration, and maintain financial records in conjunction with management and external accountant.
•	Coordinate procurement, inventory control, and distribution of office supplies, stationery, equipment, and administrative resources to ensure the office operates efficiently and effectively.
•	Manage communication with suppliers and internal stakeholders, including handling enquiries, and supporting service delivery requirements for the customers.
•	Coordinate workplace facilities, office equipment, and administrative service requirements and supplier services to support a safe and productive working environment.
•	Monitor administrative compliance requirements, maintain company documentation, support audits and reporting processes, and provide management with administrative information to assist decision-making.

Required Qualification & Experience
•	Minimum AQF Associate Diploma or Higher-level Degree in related field; and
•	A minimum of 1-year relevant experience

Salary Package: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum, commensurate with skills and experience.

Application Timeframe: 28 July 2026 to 27 August 2026. 
Interested candidates should submit their resume and cover letter. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the interview.

About the Employer
Tax Solutions New South Wales is a growing boutique accounting and advisory firm based in Parramatta. Since 2021, we have delivered high-quality, client-focused solutions across a wide range of accounting disciplines. We support small to medium-sized businesses and individuals with bookkeeping, taxation, business advisory, cash flow forecasting, and external CFO services. Our firm prides itself on accuracy, responsiveness, and personal service.

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Accountant to join our professional team and contribute to delivering expert financial guidance and compliance solutions to our expanding client base.

Key Responsibilities

Skills & Qualifications

JBS Australia is Australia's largest and most respected meat and food processing company. As part of the JBS Australia Group, Andrews Meat Industries (AMI) provides vibrant long-term career prospects.

Andrews Meat Industries is a leading food service meat supplier comprising three key divisions: foodservice, value added (cooked) and export. Across these divisions, the company supplies to all areas of the hospitality industry, including restaurants, cafes, hotels, clubs, and resort groups, as well as servicing a number of other market segments, including health and aged care, education, aviation, and sporting venues.

About the Role
There is an exciting opportunity for a Data Analyst to join our Lidcombe Site, this is a full-time role to provide data analysis, reporting and commercial support to the Commercial Business Units to facilitate informed decision-making and business performance improvement. The annual salary for this role is not less than $79,423.00 plus superannuation.

Key Responsibilities:
Generating and maintaining automation of Sales reports and functions (weekly, monthly, ad-hoc)
Help in Managing and maintaining Cost Prices and standard Prices
Assisting with ad-hoc data requests and projects as needed
Gathering data from various sources, cleaning, formatting, and preparing it for analysis. Retrieving data as requested by other team members or department

System Maintenance (Automated reports, ongoing auditing of data maintenance of program)
Updating internal and external pricing/costings
Problem solving – identifying and understanding the root cause, highlighting any risks, proposing solution, executing and/or escalating to Commercial Manager
Internal system maintenance including Inventory maintenance and creating codes for new product lines
Maintain and create effective and efficient work processes and procedures. Compile, file and complete client tender documentation
Analysing and interpreting sales, pricing and operational data to identify trends, patterns and business insights, and producing analytical reports and insights to support commercial decision-making
Collaborating with management and internal stakeholders to determine data requirements, reporting objectives and methodologies for data collection and analysis
Evaluating the accuracy, reliability and integrity of source data and implementing data validation procedures to maintain data quality standards
Performing data mining and data cleansing activities to identify trends, anomalies and opportunities for process improvements and business optimisation
Developing and maintaining dashboards, charts and visualisations to communicate analytical findings and business insights to management and stakeholders
Applying data analytical tools and techniques to transform, process and interpret business data for reporting and decision-making purposes
Utilising reporting and database tools to automate data extraction, processing and visualisation activities
Preparing analytical reports, presentations and recommendations to support strategic planning and operational decision-making

About you:
Relevant Bachelor degree or higher qualification, plus at least 1 year of full-time experience in a similar role
Advanced Excel and reporting skills (PivotTables, VLOOKUP and formulas)
Able to communicate and work with various stakeholders to understand data and support decision making
Strong data literacy
High attention to detail and accuracy
High organisational skills
Relevant experience within the manufacturing industry would be an advantage

The ad is valid for 28 days.
